newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan Navy backs single-hull tanker ban.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan Navy backs single-hull tanker ban.

text.p: Venezuela's Navy on Friday endorsed a controversial ban on single-hulled oil tankers using the Lake Maracaibo shipping channel, deepening a legal crisis which could hit the country's oil exports.

"The Navy, as an arm of the National Armed Forces, is not a deliberating body and respects the constitution and laws, therefore, it is its duty to support and fulfil judicial resolutions," the Navy said in a statement.
Judge Ricardo Colmenares banned single-hull tankers from the channel after the Greek-flagged Nissos Amorgos went aground on Feb 28, spilling at least 25,000 barrels.
Luis Giusti, president of state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela, said Thursday he hoped to resolve the problem before it is due to take effect on April 16.
"I think this is something that will be resolved because it would have a terrible effect on Venezuela," Giusti said.

The channel is used for over one million barrels per day of Venezuela's oil exports, but Venezuela has only 12 double-hulled ships which could export about 400,000 bpd from the Lake, shipping sources say.
Only about 20 percent of the world's tanker fleet has double hulls.
